column8: Sarcastic vent that everyone, even male friends, tells her what to do while pregnant.
column9: Even male friends!!! Because they have a wife/sister/mother who was pregnant and they know!!!

column8: What friends said about a concert and a work conference.
column9: this other friend butted in to say "you stay at home, you should not be going around such crowded places". Then, I was arranging to go to a work conference event, same reaction, "you're being so inconsiderate going to places with many people". Or, the classic, "uhhh should you be eating that?".

column8: Her answer to being treated as reckless.
column9: It's like most people treat you like you're this yolo teenager who's going around Johnny Knoxvilling. Excuse me! The person who's MOST concerned about my health and the health of my babies is..... myself???

column8: UK teacher near term asks whether one pregnancy sick day would trigger maternity leave early.
column9: I understand if you take a day of sick leave due to pregnancy related illness and you're within 4 weeks of due date this will/can automatically trigger mat leave. My question is, does it have to..?

column8: On her feet teaching a practical subject; wants to last until summer for pay.
column9: For pay reasons, I'm hoping to make it to the summer, but this hot weather has made me realise I might just need the odd day off here and there to recover this term

column8: Describing her classroom in the heat.
column9: my room is a disgusting sauna in hot weather

column8: Her school has not acted on an occupational health report about adjustments.
column9: I also had an occupational health appt, the report was sent a few weeks ago and I've heard not a thing from hr or SLT re the adjustments

column8: At 14 weeks with her first, told she will need a planned c-section; grieving the birth she imagined.
column9: I always dreamed of a water birth or even just to do it the way my body was made to.

column8: Thanking a commenter whose reassuring story calmed her fear of surgery.
column9: All im seeing is emergency c section horror stories and im so scared but this helped a lot

column8: At 13 weeks, still very sick all day and night after reaching the second trimester.
column9: So i’m 13 weeks pregnant, finally entered my second trimester and I still feel miserable.

column8: Money worries in an early pregnancy.
column9: Financial stress is MAJOR for us right now and he’s working for family and totally being overworked and underpaid and it’s stressing me out a lot.

column9: of course I was watching a POV of placing an epidural and made the mistake of going to the comment section🫩

column8: After moving states at 31 weeks, no OB will take her despite insurance.
column9: even with my insurance everywhere has been turning me away since 19 weeks, and my car can’t drive the interstate right now. Life’s been something else lately and so I feel like unfortunately I’ll be walking into this birth blind.

column8: At 32 weeks with a part-time desk job, exhausted and guilty about resting.
column9: i work a desk job part time and when i get home i’m exhausted most of the time and just want to lay in bed.

column8: Worried that resting more could harm the baby.
column9: i’m worried it’s going to hurt the baby or something with me not doing as much physical activity.

column8: Sent between urgent care, her OB and the ER for a painful skin reaction.
column9: I have been crying all day. I feel like I’m being passed around.

column8: Not pregnant, afraid of pregnancy and birth since school; what women in her family tell her.
column9: Even women in my family are saying i should get over it or i will end up alone, that this is a beautiful thing and that i am over reacting.

column8: Six days from her due date, family helping all day correct how she sets up her home.
column9: Every time I start something I get the, “why are you doing it that way.” “That’s not how I would organize that.” “Trust me with a baby you’ll want to do it this way.”

column8: Her family's reply when she asks to stop and rest.
column9: And I got, “Nah. This house isn’t ready for a baby.” Followed by, “we are all the help you have. Better take advantage of it.”

column8: Single mother-to-be wanting quiet before the birth.
column9: And I just want to be in my house, in the quiet, and do my nesting in peace.

column8: Her mother refusing to wrap up for the day.
column9: I literally said, “Okay. Let’s wrap it up. I’m done for today.” And my mom said, “yeah. Well I’m not!” 🫠

column8: At 32 weeks a specialist told her she had gained too much, against her midwife's view.
column9: she looks at me and says “you’ve gained a LOT of weight. Way too much weight and should be focused on a diet until he comes. He is a very large baby.”

column8: The specialist cuts her off when she cites her midwife.
column9: I say “my midwife told me last week I’m in the healthy range and–“ […] “no no this is way too much she’s wrong. You need to cut out carbohydrates and sugar completely. Lay off the pizza and cookies ok?”

column8: At 19 weeks, unhappy with facial puffiness in photos.
column9: I bought a guasha tool but not sure if it’s helping.

column8: At almost 20 weeks the tiredness came back.
column9: I had energy from weeks 10-16 but after that its like my exhaustion returned. I thought 2nd trimester was the honeymoon trimester but I dont feel it right now 😭

column8: First-time mother on the first trimester; post reads possibly tool-polished, one voice.
column9: nobody prepared me for how HARD the first trimester could feel. 😭 The nonstop sleeping, nausea, mood swings, feeling guilty for not working or being productive 24/7… it’s a lot mentally and physically.

column8: Replying about her first trimester and work.
column9: This 1st trimester has it impossible for me to work I cannot stay awake for the life of me hehe

column8: Congested since 10 weeks, now 20.
column9: I’m getting so tired of not being able to breathe normally.

column8: Stocking up before any nausea, still afraid of being sick at work and on the tram.
